definition: the quiet office, the earbuds, and the noise I put over the top

settled:
The office is in the basement at the far corner of the house, below ground and as far from the common rooms as it can be. Two layers of quiet, designed rather than lucky.

The AirPods go in when I leave it for somewhere noisier. Full cancelling is the default, and I pull one earbud out when I need to hear.

The earbuds hurt after a while. The seal presses on the ear canal, the pressure builds the longer they are in, and lying on that side stacks head pressure on top. So the office carries the hours they cannot.

When cancelling still leaves a costly residue I put the dark noise from the phone over the top. It masks rather than cancels, raising the floor evenly so the residue stops standing out. Sometimes, not by default.

Volume is the main trigger. Pencils and chalk cost me whatever the volume, and cancelling helps least with exactly those. It takes out steady low sound far better than a sudden high scratch.

Music for pleasure comes through the office speakers, never the earbuds.
